how: A token charge is an ordinary Cost and Usage row. ServiceCategory is "AI and Machine Learning", ConsumedUnit is "Tokens" and ConsumedQuantity counts them. PricingQuantity and PricingUnit say how they were priced, which can be in blocks, such as per million tokens.

Which model, and which kind of token, are recorded inside one JSON column, SkuPriceDetails, as FOCUS-defined properties. ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily, ModelId and ModelVersion describe the model. TokenDirection (input or output) and TokenCacheAction (uncached, cache read, cache write) describe the tokens. All six are new in the 1.5 candidate.
Who made the request can be recorded in three columns, also new in 1.5: PrincipalId, CredentialId and RequesterDetails, for example the service account or API key behind the calls.
Everything else, such as cost, currency, period and provider, uses the same columns as any other charge.

feature.description: FOCUS enables normalization of usage-based billing data from artificial intelligence and machine learning services, including token consumption for AI model APIs. Token quantities are represented through consumption and pricing columns, allowing consumption and cost to be tracked by [*SKU*](#glossary:sku), token direction, and cache interaction. The TokenDirection and TokenCacheAction properties of [SkuPriceDetails](#datamodel.costandusage.skupricedetails) label the direction of the metered tokens and their interaction with a cache, so those attributes can be compared across service providers independently of provider-specific meter names, with model identity carried in the same SkuPriceDetails object.

rows.description: Name of the entity that created the model
Grouping of related models as defined by the model developer
Identifier for the model as it appears in billing, which may be namespaced by the service provider and is not guaranteed to match across service providers
Version of the model within a given model family, as defined by the model developer
Interaction of the metered tokens with a cache
Direction of the metered tokens, into or out of the model

properties.note: TokenDirection applies to SKUs that meter tokens in one direction only, and TokenCacheAction to SKUs that meter only tokens consumed from a request. The requirements above state when each property applies and what each value identifies. A SKU that bills request tokens on one meter whether or not they were served from or placed into a cache carries no TokenCacheAction, because "Uncached" would misdescribe the tokens that interacted with the cache, and TokenDirection still identifies its tokens as input. Because null is not one of the allowed values, TokenCacheAction is omitted rather than set to null when the interaction of the metered tokens with a cache is not known. [Consumed Quantity](#datamodel.costandusage.consumedquantity) requirements state that a token counted on a "Read" or "Write" row is not also counted on a row that carries neither value. The model developer defines which cache interactions and which token directions a model distinguishes. Which of those a service provider meters as its own charge, and the meter name it uses, vary across service providers and across model versions, so each property identifies one attribute of the metered tokens independently of how a given service provider names its meters. Reasoning tokens are generated in a response, so a SKU that meters them separately carries TokenDirection "Output". Dimensions that qualify a charge without describing the direction of its tokens or their interaction with a cache, such as token modality, reasoning effort, cache retention duration, and context window size, are not values of these properties. [Examples: AI Prompt Caching](#appendix.examples:aipromptcaching) shows both properties on two service providers that meter cache activity differently.

gaps.title: The token details are optional
gaps.text: SkuPriceDetails is a conditional column that may be empty even when a price is identified, and the model and token properties are recommendations (SHOULD), not requirements. A provider can conform without them, so comparing token costs across providers depends on each one choosing to fill them in.

quotes.text: SkuPriceDetails MAY be null when SkuPriceId is not null.
SkuPriceDetails SHOULD include TokenDirection when the *SKU Price* meters only input or only output tokens.

gaps.title: They sit inside a JSON column
gaps.text: The working group chose properties inside SkuPriceDetails over new columns (#2018, #2442), and newer proposals follow the same pattern, such as region scope (#2613). That keeps the column list stable, but every token query has to unpack JSON. The specification's queries use BigQuery's JSON_VALUE, which other databases write differently: the lab runs them in DuckDB through a small json_value macro.

quotes.text: Similar JSON functions are widely available across major SQL engines with variances in syntax, so the examples may need to be adapted for other database engines.

gaps.title: Models and tokens don't line up across providers
gaps.text: The same model can carry a different ModelId from each seller, and a token is not a fixed amount of content. So a cost per million tokens compares prices, not work done, and comparing one model across providers needs ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily and ModelVersion filled in as well.

quotes.text: ModelId: Identifier for the model as it appears in billing, which may be namespaced by the service provider and is not guaranteed to match across service providers.
The amount of content a single token represents is determined by the model, so token counts are not directly comparable across models.

gaps.title: Pricing dimensions not covered yet
gaps.text: The specification names dimensions that the token properties deliberately leave out, and each has an open request. Others have been raised since: processing tiers such as batch or priority, provisioned throughput, regional prices and finer AI service subcategories. A query for what caching saves was taken out until the SKU Price dataset can supply the uncached price (#2702).

quotes.text: Dimensions that qualify a charge without describing the direction of its tokens or their interaction with a cache, such as token modality, reasoning effort, cache retention duration, and context window size, are not values of these properties.

gaps.title: No public data with token charges yet
gaps.text: Only the specification's worked examples contain token rows. The token queries return nothing on the accepted 1.0 sample or on the samples proposed for 1.3 and 1.4, so no public FOCUS sample data yet shows token billing.

gaps.title: Nothing yet on energy, utilisation or results
gaps.text: FOCUS records what was charged. The specification has no column or property for energy use or emissions, for how busy the resources behind a charge were, or for what the tokens produced. The request that added model identity (#2018) left operational telemetry out of scope. Open requests would cover parts of this: sustainability measures, a companion utilisation dataset (which absorbed a request for AI and GPU utilisation), a mapping from OpenTelemetry, and costs for work that never reached a billed SKU.

quotes.text: Those belong in observability tooling, not cost and usage data.
quotes.context: The model identity request's own scope, on latency, CPU use and sampling settings
